summary.name: Anime (Drawing and Illustration category; provenance explicit). The source directly names this visual direction.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit: anime character design with stable proportions, expressive poses, clean linework and controlled shadow shapes. Key poses, holds and selectively detailed action carry the motion. A static cel-shading filter is explicitly not character animation.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: the source names character-led anime work and recommends layered backgrounds for openings, character introductions and scenic establishing shots. Inferred: fits illustrated video or interactive HTML built from prepared drawings. Audience and objective are unspecified.
summary.limitations: Explicit: consistent character drawings or frame sequences are required, and missing character assets must be reported rather than replaced by a filter. Parallax alone must not fake character animation, anime design languages must not be mixed, and depth must not be over-blurred. Frame-review evidence covers only one example video at seconds 1–8.
summary.palette: Example tokens, not approved exact colors: background #F4EFE5, foreground #293447, accent_1 #668DA0, accent_2 #C47C67. Background policy is scene_dependent, so backgrounds should follow the subject, lighting and mood. Foreground on background measures 10.931:1; accents (3.509 and 3.833) are decorative only. Gradients are disabled. Task-supplied or approved colors override these tokens. The sampled reference shows a fixed neutral character over changing background families, which is an example rather than a style rule.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Video motion derives from seekable composition time; interactive HTML may add scroll or pointer input. Optional references: motion-006 gives bounded pupil following with delayed brows, a slight tilt and blinks, requiring eye layers or a rig; motion-012 gives a progress-controlled chapter handoff; motion-015 gives narrative steps. Use only references the scene supports. Gaze is illustrated character animation, not viewer tracking. Preserve deliberate cuts and reading holds.
summary.audio: Audio direction is unspecified in the source: no genre, tempo, voice, effects or mandatory layer is assigned. Propose choices from topic, audience and storyboard, stating assumptions, and honor explicit user audio and supplied assets. Do not default silently to instrumental music or invent audio files. Keep speech intelligible and allow silence where reading holds need it.
summary.assetRequirements: Requires prepared, consistent character drawings or numbered transparent PNG frame sequences with alpha, uniform dimensions and clear layer naming. Krita is optional for drawing and PNG-sequence export. Motion-006 needs suitable eye layers or a rig. No uploads are promised; load local fonts and assets before composition and report any missing character assets.
summary.combinations: style-101 suits background-layer parallax behind held character poses, sharing one lighting direction and keeping character proportions fixed during camera moves. style-112 suits HUD overlays only inside sci-fi device frames, using #293447, #668DA0 and #C47C67 with no neon additions and line weight matching the anime linework. Keep anime alone unless layered backgrounds or diegetic interfaces are needed.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default pipeline for scene assembly, timing, audio synchronization and export; Remotion is a fallback only when a verified limitation applies and the reason is recorded. The source leaves style renderer and motion engine unspecified, so choose them from the style: prepared drawings or PNG sequences, with GSAP as a paused, seekable timeline. chroma-js is optional for contrast checks. Validate with check, snapshot and render commands.
